lyrics:
[Intro: soft piano, handclaps, a wordless vocal line]

[Verse 1: female voice, low and controlled]
I had it how I liked it
White couch, quiet, mine
Every glass put back in order
Every evening on a line
I'd decided I was finished
I had told myself I'm fine

[Pre-Chorus: drums enter, voice rising]
Then a caseworker's car in the drive
One backpack and two wide eyes

[Chorus: full band, voice soaring]
The day you came through the door
Every wall I'd made forgot what it was for
Jelly on the white couch, shoes across the floor
The whole house learned your name
The day you came through the door

[Verse 2: voice warmer, bass moving]
You asked me where the bathroom was
You asked me could you leave the light
You asked me, very quiet,
How long, and I said, "Tonight,"
Then I said, "As long as you like,"
And heard my own voice, and it was right

[Pre-Chorus: drums build]
Seven years old and a paper bag
You carried in the only thing I didn't have

[Chorus: full band, voice soaring]
The day you came through the door
Every wall I'd made forgot what it was for
Jelly on the white couch, shoes across the floor
The whole house learned your name
The day you came through the door

[Bridge: half-time, choir pad, voice at full power]
I thought I was the one saying yes
I thought I was the rescue
Oh, I thought I was the rescue

[Final Chorus: highest, ad-libs, handclaps doubled]
The day you came through the door
Every wall I'd made forgot what it was for
Drawings on the fridge now, laughing down the hall
The whole house knows your name
You came through the door, and you're home

[Outro: piano, a small voice: "Can I call you Mom?"]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 80 BPM, 4/4, A major. Slow, heavy and uplifting, with a steady clap on every backbeat.

VOICE: Female, a big, agile R&B-pop voice held back in the verses and opened fully in the choruses, with runs and held high notes. Stacked harmonies of her own voice. Free ad-libs over the last chorus. A child speaks the final line.

INSTRUMENTS: Piano, handclaps, a deep, booming kick and a wide snare, a sustained bass, a string section, a choir-like synth pad, a wordless vocal sample used as a motif.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:48 Pre-chorus. 0:58 Chorus 1. 1:28 Verse 2. 2:02 Pre-chorus. 2:12 Chorus 2. 2:42 Bridge, half-time. 3:02 Final chorus. 3:36 Outro, piano and a child's question at 3:54.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-2000s pop-R&B power ballad: huge drums, shimmering pads, piano bright, vocal enormous and central.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'Oh, I thought I was the rescue' at 2:52.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original praises a lover. A woman in her forties who has arranged a life without need can be undone the same way by a child, and the bridge admits who saved whom.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Guarded, startled, opened, claimed.
